San Francisco neighbourhoods by bike

The Toronto-to-SF neighbourhood matches, joined into one ride from Hotel VIA at 138 King St
Distance
38.5 km
Total climbing
384 m
Stops
6
Riding time
2h24–3h13
Straight answer: this does not fit three hours. 38.5 km with 384 m of climbing is 2h24m–3h13m of pedaling alone (c: 55% on the pace range). Ride it as a half-day, 4–4½ hour outing with real stops, or take one of the trims further down. The good news: the route is sequenced so the two big descents come at the end of the hardest sections.

The pairings

TorontoSan FranciscoThe shared quality
Rosedale1Pacific Heights (c: 75%)Old money, grand houses, quiet streets, walkable to downtown
High Park-Swansea2Inner Sunset (c: 70%)Leafy family residential wrapped around a huge park — Golden Gate Park plays the High Park role almost exactly
Roncesvalles3Noe Valley (c: 60%)Gentrified main-street strip, indie shops, stroller density
Danforth / Greektown4Inner Richmond (c: 65%)A long, still-working immigrant commercial spine (Clement St). North Beach is the tourist-facing version
Leslieville5Bernal Heights (c: 60%)Ex-working-class, now young families and brunch, with Cortland Ave as its Queen St E
The Beaches6Outer Sunset (c: 60%)Beach-town-inside-a-city, relaxed. Though The Beaches is far more affluent — that side is closer to Marina/Cow Hollow

Pins sit on each neighbourhood's geocoded centroid, so they mark the area's rough middle rather than its high street.

The Hotel VIA → Bernal Heights leg is the one that will hurt — 118 m of climbing with pitches over 10%. If you want it easier, approach Bernal from the north on Folsom rather than the east side. Inner Sunset → Outer Sunset is the reward: 4.25 km with zero climbing and a 69 m drop to the ocean.

If you want it to fit three hours

A. Drop Outer Sunset

30.3 km, 335 m climbing — 1h53m–2h31m riding, leaving 30–65 min of stop time. Cut straight north through Golden Gate Park from Inner Sunset to Inner Richmond.

Costs you the ocean and the best descent on the route.

B. Drop Bernal Heights

35.2 km, 314 m climbing — 2h12m–2h56m riding. Removes the single hardest climb but saves less distance.

Only marginally inside three hours — workable if you ride briskly and stop briefly.

C. Keep all six, skip the return leg

32.6 km to Pacific Heights — then Muni or a rideshare back to South Beach rather than the final 5.9 km. Ends on the Pacific Heights high point with the whole city below you.

Assumptions worth checking

• Pace range assumes 12–16 km/h average including lights and climbs (c: 55%). SF's hills make average speed far less predictable than Toronto's flat grid.
• The routing engine available to me does not use a true bicycle profile, so I steered the route by hand through known low-grade corridors — the Wiggle, the Panhandle, Lincoln Way, the Great Highway, Lake Street. Cross-check the turn-by-turn in Google Maps before riding (c: 70% that it matches what a local would choose).
• Elevation figures come from a 10 m bare-earth model, so total climbing is accurate to maybe ±10% (c: 75%).
• Stops are the commercial hearts of each neighbourhood — Cortland Ave, 24th St, 9th & Irving, Judah & 45th, Clement St, Fillmore & Sacramento — not geographic centroids.
